title: Weekly KPI Check-in - Lina Garcia - 2026-03-09
content:
WEEKLY PERSONAL KPI CHECK-IN (draft)
Date: 2026-03-09
Owner: Lina Garcia (eng-serving-runtime)
Context: personal tracking doc for weekly progress against my OKRs/KPIs. Mostly for my own notes and to share quick sync points with Avery/Noah.

OKR alignment (short):
- Objective: Improve inference latency & stability for common small-batch text generation workloads (core product goal).
  - KR1: Reduce p95 token-generation latency for 2-sentence prompts on gtx-cluster from 90ms -> 70ms by end of Q2.
  - KR2: Ship KV-cache improvements to reduce cold-start cost by 25% and instrumented coverage for cache hit breakdowns.
  - KR3: Deploy canary for kernel-selection feature to 5% traffic and validate no regression in quality or tail latency.

This week's status summary (what I did):
- Spiked an alternative kernel-selection heuristic (PR #3421) and ran local perf runs. Median looks good; p95 improvement ~8-12% on the short-sequence microbenchmarks.
- Finished integration tests for KV-cache eviction scenario and added an additional regression test to catch stale-cache misses. Test coverage increased +4% for the cache module.
- Landed telemetry hooks for per-route cache-hit ratios; initial dashboards in Console (linked above) show ~6% cache hit on dev traffic which is lower than expected (need followups).
- Coordinated with Release Eng to plan canary rollout; tentative date 2026-03-16 pending SRE signoff.

Metrics / quick numbers:
- Baseline p95 (2-sentence prompt, current prod model on gtx-cluster): 90ms (goal 70ms)
- This week's experimental p95 (kernel-select spike): 78-82ms across 3 runs (promising, need wider testing)
- Cache hit rate (dev traffic): 6% (target for initial improvement phase: 25%)
- Test coverage (cache package): was 62% -> now 66%

Blockers / risks:
- Cache hit rate low because dev traffic is too synthetic; need a replay from real synthetic workloads or sampled production traces (waiting on privacy approval).
- Kernel selection improvement regresses memory footprint slightly in one config; need perf-engineering signoff and longer soak tests.
- Release scheduling: canary depends on infra window and SRE availability; if postponed, slows KR3 progress.

Next actions (this coming week):
- Work with Data Platform to get a sanitized request-replay (INF-1302) for more realistic cache-hit estimates. (Owner: Lina)
- Run the kernel-select variant across more instance types (a100, t4) and different sequence-length distributions; capture p50/p95 and memory. (Owner: Lina)
- Create a small automated job to compute per-route cache-hit ratios daily and emit an alert if below 15% for two consecutive days. (Owner: Noah / Lina)
- Prepare canary runbook and rollback criteria for the 2026-03-16 tentative rollout; share with SRE and Release Eng. (Owner: Lina / Avery)

Notes / ideas to capture (brainstorming):
- Could we add a small in-memory prefix shard to warm caches for high-reuse routes? Tradeoff: memory vs early hits.
- Consider a two-tier kernel selection: default fast path + fallback accuracy path when memory headroom detected. Might reduce p95 for common cases while preserving quality.

Quick status for personal growth KPIs:
- Mentorship: 1:1 with mentee scheduled weekly; covered debugging practices and perf regression triage this week.
- Documentation: drafted a short intern-facing doc for cache behavior; needs a pass for clarity.

Open questions I want to discuss with manager/peers:
- Prioritize cache-hit improvements (longer term data work) vs kernel-micro-optimizations (quick wins). Which gives better delta for Q2?
- Any objections to proceeding with a 5% canary on 2026-03-16 if SRE approves?

This is a working doc - will update after replay data arrives and after the broader perf run on Friday.

---
Version notes: initial draft 2026-03-09. Will convert to a short digest for manager sync if there are meaningful pivots.
